nodes.summary: Let $p_1 = 2, p_2 = 3, p_3 = 5, \dots$ be the prime numbers in increasing order. For every natural number $k > 4$, the square of the $(k+1)$-st prime is smaller than the product of the first $k$ primes: $p_{k+1}^2 < p_1 p_2 \cdots p_k$.
nodes.title: Bonse's inequality

nodes.summary: The sixth prime number, counting $2$ as the first, is $13$.
nodes.title: The sixth prime is thirteen

nodes.summary: For every $k \ge 1$, the $k$-th smallest prime number exists and is prime.
nodes.title: The enumeration of the primes takes prime values

nodes.summary: For $k \ge 1$ let $p_k$ be the $k$-th smallest prime number. If $i < j$, then $p_i < p_j$.
nodes.title: The enumeration of the primes is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: Let $p_1 < p_2 < p_3 < \cdots$ be the prime numbers in increasing order. For every $k \ge 1$, $p_{k+1} < 2 p_k$.
nodes.title: Bertrand's postulate for consecutive primes

nodes.summary: The set of prime natural numbers is infinite.
nodes.title: Infinitely many primes

nodes.summary: Let $a_0 < a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers and write $A_n = a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{n-1}$ for the product of its first $n$ terms. If there is a real number $c > 2$ such that $\log A_n / \log a_n > c$ for all sufficiently large $n$, then $a$ is a Bonse sequence.
nodes.title: A sufficient condition for a Bonse sequence

nodes.summary: For $m \ge 1$ let $p_m$ be the $m$-th prime, so that $p_1 = 2$, and set $p_0 = 2$. A sequence $a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots$ of natural numbers is a Bonse sequence if $p_{a_n}^2 < p_{a_0} p_{a_1} \cdots p_{a_{n-1}}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
nodes.title: Bonse sequence of prime indices

nodes.summary: Let $a_0 < a_1 < a_2 < \cdots$ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers and write $A_n = a_0 a_1 \cdots a_{n-1}$ for the product of its first $n$ terms. Suppose that $(n + 1) \log \log a_n / \log a_{n+1} \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$, and that there is a real number $c < 2$ such that $\log A_n / \log a_n < c$ for infinitely many $n$. Then $a$ is not a Bonse sequence.
nodes.title: A sufficient condition for a non-Bonse sequence

nodes.summary: For $m \ge 1$, $p_m$ is the $m$-th prime, so that $p_1 = 2$, $p_2 = 3$, $p_3 = 5$; at $m = 0$ the value is also $2$.
nodes.title: The $m$-th prime, counted from one

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
